NREF is a small-cap (~$0.36B) externally-managed mortgage REIT lending into life science (39.4%), multifamily (37.6%), SFR (15.1%), storage/industrial/marina. It pays a $2.00/sh common dividend (12.9% yield) covered ~1.0–1.2× by CAD. The stock trades at 0.83× book and the market is pricing it as a slow credit bleed; my evidence says CAD is stable-to-modestly-growing and the common deserves a lower required return than the price implies.

## SECTION 1 — MACRO
- **Rates are the dominant variable.** rf (10y) 5.28%, real 2.92%, breakeven 2.36%; curve +0.47% and steepening; IG spread 1.47%, HY OAS 3.10% [DATA 1.5]. For a mREIT, higher rates compress mark-to-market on fixed-rate loans (bear) but keep new-origination spreads wide (bull). NREF funded SOFR+900 and 14.0%-fixed coupons in Q2'26 [PRIMARY P1], so spread capture is strong; the Mizuho TRS at SOFR+245 is floating cost that rises with rates.
